    "text": "Prioritize a bounded replay-controller experiment around a frozen ADAM checkpoint. Compare fixed, hand-written adaptive and replay-improved policies on sandboxed repair tasks. No training, deployment, work-item dispatch or architecture change is part of this harvest.\n\nThe 162x headline compares different model-backed systems. The controlled Lasso comparison is 550 versus 317 discovery-agent calls; replay improvement does not guarantee future improvement or equivalent total-cost savings.     "text": "3. Dream-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Worlds\nAs shown in Figure 1, Dream-RSI alternates between online exploration and offline “dreaming” to\nimprove an executable exploration policy that allocates discovery computation. During the online phase,\nthe policy guides a fixed discovery agent, while a fixed evaluator scores the resulting candidates and\nprovides diagnostic feedback. The resulting discovery tree serves as a replay world in which alternative\npolicies can be evaluated using recorded outcomes. A fixed LLM-based policy-development agent uses\nthis feedback to revise the exploration policy code, and the best evaluated version is deployed for the\nnext online rollout. Only the exploration-policy code changes; the underlying models, evaluator, and\nexecution interfaces remain fixed.\n\n4\n\f                            Dream-RSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Worlds",

    "text": "Figure 1 | Overview of Dream-RSI. The system operates in a recursive self-improvement loop via\nthree core stages: 1\n                   O Online Explore, where the current exploration policy guides a coding agent\nto expand a discovery tree and log historical traces; O  2 Construct Replay Simulator, where the\ngenerated discovery tree is converted into a reusable simulator pool; and O3 Dreaming-based Policy\nImprovement, where the agent \"dreams\" up a massive pool of alternative policies in its mind. It\nthen feeds these candidate policies into the replay simulator to simulate executions and derive rapid\nfeedback, continuously refining its strategy (detailed in the Zoom-in box). The updated policy then\nredeploys for the next round of online exploration.",
